newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nobel laureate congratulates compatriots on prize.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate congratulates compatriots on prize.

text.p: Nobel Peace Prize laureate Rigoberta Menchu of Guatemala on Wednesday congratulated her countrymen Alvaro Arzu and Rolando Moran for being awarded UNESCO's 1996 peace award.

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation said on Wednesday its Felix Houphouet-Boigny peace prize would be shared between Guatemalan president Arzu and Moran, leader of the rebel group with whom he signed an agreement in December ending decades of civil war.
Menchu, in Brussels for an international aid donor conference on Guatemala, told Reuters the award honoured all Guatemalans.
"I am very happy to hear this," she said. "It is, I am sure, in recognition for the whole Guatemalan society and also for the hard work on all parts for peace."
The award, sometimes called the "little Nobel" because it is awarded several months before the Nobel prize, is named after the long-serving first president of Ivory Coast, who died in 1993.
Menchu was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992 for her efforts in helping to preserve indiginous Guatemalan society during 36 years of civil war.
Some 140,000 people were killed or "disappeared" during the conflict, most of them in the Cold War years of the 1980s, before the peace accord was signed on December 29.
The UNESCO award's first joint laureates were South Africa's then opposition leader Nelson Mandela and president Frederick De Klerk for agreeing to end apartheid.

In 1993, UNESCO was first to reward the Israeli-PLO peace agreement by giving its prize to the late Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin, his foreign minister Shimon Peres and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat. They later won the Nobel Peace Prize.
